newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt has five offers for Amriyah Cement.
newsitem.headline: Egypt has five offers for Amriyah Cement.

text.p: The Egyptian state has received five offers from strategic investors to buy 40 percent of the shares in Amriyah Cement, an official of the state holding company said on Monday.
The eight million shares would be worth 432 million pounds ($127 million) at the market price of 54 pounds a share.

Wadi Mishraqi of the state's Holding Company for Metallurgical Industries, who is handling the sale, said the offers were from three international cement producers and from two local Egyptian consortia.
He declined to name them, saying the choice of buyer would be taken in complete secrecy within about two weeks.
The holding company owns about 72.5 percent of Amriyah Cement after several sales to the public under the government's privatisation programme.

The cement company made a net after-tax profit of 150.9 million pounds in the financial year 1995/6, up from 133.755 million in the previous year. The years end on June 30. The dividend for the year will be not less than 5.00 pounds, against 4.50 for the previous year, the company says.
